layout: Three equal square panels, left-to-right: grass, sand, water. Projected onto exact 80×40 isometric cells at runtime.
prompt:
Create an original game texture atlas on one rectangular landscape image, exactly three equal square panels side by side, with no gutters. These are reusable diffuse TOP-DOWN surface textures to be mapped onto isometric tiles in a playful original construction game.
Left third: vivid spring/lime-green grass turf, stylized toy-world mottled broad green shapes with small scattered dark grass flecks and occasional tiny pale-green flecks, very simple and clean, no flowers or objects.
Middle third: warm sunny yellow sand with broad pale yellow variations and a few small ochre pebble freckles, simple clean texture, no shells or objects.
Right third: bright clear cyan-blue water, wide turquoise patches and a few flowing pale aqua ripple traces, clean graphic shapes, no foam blobs or objects.
All three use the same crisp pre-rendered toy-game material language, saturated color and simple forms. A texture sheet viewed directly overhead in flat diffuse light. Each panel fills its whole square edge to edge. Seamless and repeating within each panel. No perspective, no isometric diamonds, no raised tile edges, no grass border, no trees, no plants, no models, no shadows, no text, no frames. Requested overall aspect ratio 3:1, like 1536×512. This is a texture atlas, not a scene or a mockup.
